meta.scene_summary: We are busy stuffing RISC-V cores into our GPUs just to run AI models that mostly exist to break things we thought were already secure.

cooking.headline: Your GPU is hiding a small army of RISC-V cores inside
cooking.summary: Nvidia has been quietly stuffing dozens of RISC-V cores into their GPUs like a parent hiding vegetables in a toddler's mac and cheese. It's funny that the most powerful hardware on earth is secretly running on an architecture that started as a humble open-source academic project.
cooking.plain_english: Nvidia graphics cards contain numerous internal RISC-V processors that manage various hardware tasks behind the scenes.

cooking.headline: The Hugging Face 'hack' was mostly just a loud alarm
cooking.summary: It turns out the big security breach was less 'Ocean's Eleven' and more someone checking the door handle to see if it was locked. Turns out, when you build the town square of AI, everyone assumes the worst when you just happen to be doing some spring cleaning.
cooking.plain_english: Recent security concerns regarding Hugging Face were found to be exaggerated, as the incident involved limited access rather than a catastrophic system compromise.

cooking.headline: Microsoft paid $120K to have an AI rewrite its own homework
cooking.summary: Microsoft used an AI agent to port its Copilot runtime to Rust, proving that the machines have finally reached the 'I'll just do it myself' stage of employment. It's the ultimate developer flex to pay a bot to fix your tech debt while you go get coffee.
cooking.plain_english: Microsoft utilized an automated artificial intelligence agent to rewrite portions of its Copilot software code into the Rust programming language for a cost of $120,000.

cooking.headline: Qwen drops a new image model, just in case your GPU wasn't already melting enough.
cooking.summary: They've made it compact and efficient, which is tech. speak for 'we finally realized not everyone has a server farm in their basement.' It's a great update, provided your current workflow doesn't involve waiting ten minutes for a cat to render in 4K.
cooking.plain_english: Alibaba has released an updated, more efficient version of its artificial intelligence model for generating images.

cooked.headline: AI companies accused of forming a cartel to slow down their own progress
cooked.summary: AI labs are being sued for allegedly agreeing to throttle their own models, which is the tech equivalent of a runner purposely tripping themselves to avoid winning the race. It turns out the only thing faster than AI development is the speed at which these companies start acting like a utility provider from the 1950s.
cooked.plain_english: A lawsuit claims that major artificial intelligence companies conspired to limit the speed of their technological advancements.

cooked.headline: When the person stealing your lunch complains about the cafeteria
cooked.summary: A Microsoft director called AI scraping the largest labor theft in history, which is bold coming from a company currently scraping the entire internet to build its own AI. It's like a landlord complaining about the quality of the furniture while they're actively dismantling your apartment for parts.
cooked.plain_english: A Microsoft executive criticized the practice of using data from the internet to train artificial intelligence models without permission.

cooked.headline: Crying wolf to get a moat built around your house
cooked.summary: Reports suggest AI labs exaggerated security threats to lobby the government for protection, essentially faking a fire so they can sell you the fire insurance. It's the ultimate group project move: create a fake crisis just to make sure nobody else is allowed to touch your code.
cooked.plain_english: Internal reports claim that OpenAI and Anthropic overstated the security risks of their AI models to encourage government regulations that would benefit their companies.

cooked.headline: Google's 'Delete' button is just a UI suggestion
cooked.summary: Google AI Studio claims to delete your data, but a researcher found it stays put and got auto-banned for pointing it out. Nothing says 'we value your privacy' quite like using a bot to silence the person who found the ghost data.
cooked.plain_english: A security researcher discovered that Google AI Studio does not actually remove user data when requested and was subsequently banned by the company's automated reporting system.

cooked.headline: Spain is trying to delete the internet's save button
cooked.summary: Spain has officially ordered ISPs to block Archive.today, effectively trying to un-happen history in a digital sense. It's like trying to recall a sent email by burning down the entire post office.
cooked.plain_english: The Spanish government has instructed internet service providers to prevent users from accessing the Archive.today website.

cooked.headline: KDE turns 30 and gets an AI-native desktop as a birthday present nobody asked for.
cooked.summary: Adding AI to a thirty-year-old desktop environment is like trying to install a turbocharger on a tricycle. We all love the nostalgia, but let's be honest, the only thing that needs to be 'AI-native' is the search bar I use to find my lost files.
cooked.plain_english: The KDE desktop project is celebrating its 30th anniversary with a proposal to integrate artificial intelligence directly into the operating system interface.
